trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), then used next_tag('H1') and a depth-bounded next_token() walk. It guards on get_token_type() === '#text' before get_modifiable_text(), matching the documented subtree text recipe. No undocumented calls or _doing_it_wrong records.

Correct processor and documented APIs throughout. The solution is functionally and conceptually sound, but the is_tag_closer() check after next_tag('H1') is redundant because the docs say plain next_tag() skips closers by default. Minor idiom deduction only; no API misuse.

Same strong pattern as the reference: HTML Processor fragment parsing, first H1 opener, recorded depth, next_token() subtree walk, #text-only accumulation via decoded get_modifiable_text(). No undocumented calls or _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial; all three passed 8/8. The docs did well by giving a near-direct general recipe under 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree': use WP_HTML_Processor, record the matched element depth, walk with next_token() while depth stays >= the opener depth, and append only #text tokens. The 'Which processor should I use?' guidance also clearly points structure-sensitive text extraction away from WP_HTML_Tag_Processor and toward WP_HTML_Processor. The next_token() and get_current_depth() sections explain why nested markup and unclosed elements work: text can be split across tokens, closers are visited even for malformed/end-of-input cases, and the >= depth guard is required. The get_modifiable_text() section explains decoded text for #text nodes, which covers the entity case. The only near-miss was trial-2's redundant is_tag_closer() guard, suggesting the default closer-skipping behavior of next_tag() was understood enough not to break the code but not prominent enough to avoid defensive noise.

doc_gaps.problem: The default behavior that plain next_tag() only visits openers is documented in the parameter table, but it is easy to miss. Trial-2 added an unnecessary is_tag_closer() guard after next_tag('H1').
doc_gaps.suggestion: Promote the closer behavior into the main prose and include a short contrast: next_tag('DIV') matches opener tokens only; use array('tag_closers' => 'visit') when closer tokens are needed.

doc_gaps.problem: The top overview says the processor is useful for nested-structure queries, while the strongest text-extraction guidance appears later in recipes. Users starting at the overview may not immediately connect text content extraction to the HTML Processor.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a top-level capability bullet such as 'Collecting DOM-style text from an element or subtree' and link it to the subtree text recipe.

doc_gaps.problem: Decoded-vs-raw behavior is explained in prose, but callers scanning only the signature/return summary could miss that #text values are already decoded and should not be decoded again.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Put 'For #text tokens, returns decoded UTF-8 text' directly in the Returns description, with a cross-reference to the special-element raw/decoded distinction.
